items.statement: Introducing Lean standard work for catheter removal, one hospital at a time, lowers catheter days per 100 patient days by at least 25 percent within six months of each hospital's start, relative to that hospital's own baseline and to hospitals not yet started.
items.rationale: Need is high after two bacteraemias; novelty is low because nurse-driven removal is established (c1), which suits improvement work; the staggered design follows the coach constraint (c4).
items.risks: Secular decline across the region; loss of momentum after the coach moves on.

items.statement: Reinsertion within 72 hours stays below 6 percent of removals after each start.
items.rationale: Balancing measure with a published reference value (c6).

items.statement: The share of catheters without a documented indication falls from about 32 percent to under 10 percent.
items.rationale: Directly targets the handoff failure found in the value stream map (c3).
items.risks: Documentation may improve without catheters coming out sooner.

summary: Three hypotheses; h1 selected, h2 as the balancing check and h3 as a process measure.
